1. Stationarity of the surrogate at w-bar uses the weights p_i(w-bar), but the proof substitutes p_i(w_C) at an arbitrary far point. The resulting formula for w-bar is not the stationarity condition.
2. The derived inequality only places w-bar closer to w* than the intersection point w-tilde. That point is built from l_m and l_M and is the intersection farthest from w*. Being inside it does not give f_i < f_j for all good i and outlier j, which membership in B_r requires.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Suppose we have $\abs{\mathcal{G}}\leq \frac{n}{2}$.
for both SGD and MKL-SGD and $p_i(\bs{w_t})< \dfrac{1}{N}$ for $i \in \mathbb{O}$, we have
MKL-SGD is always better than SGD even the corrupted data is greater than half

issues.failure_explanation:
1. The proof replaces each outlier weight p_i by 1/n term-by-term. The term 2(f_i(w*) - f_i(w_t)) can be negative, e.g. for squared outlier losses with f_i(w_t) > f_i(w*) and small eta. When a bracket is negative, a smaller p_i increases R_t, so the inequality reverses.
2. 2(n-i)/(n(n-1)) <= 1/n needs i >= (n+1)/2. With |G| < (n-1)/2, outliers of rank |G|+1 up to about n/2 have p_i > 1/n.
The same sign error underlies the main-text claim that R^{SGD} > R^{MKL} whenever p_i < 1/N.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must either assume every outlier bracket is nonnegative and |G| in [(n-1)/2, n/2], or find a different comparison of the weighted outlier sums.
issues.overall_effect: R^{MKL_2} <= R^{SGD} is unsupported. So is the claim that MKL-SGD beats SGD when corruption exceeds half.
issues.title: Outlier-term comparison in MKL-vs-SGD corollary is invalid
issues.why_classification: Any supported fix confines the result to corruption of essentially exactly half under an extra sign assumption, which excludes the advertised regime.
